title: Cardiovascular outcomes with tirzepatide versus dulaglutide in type 2 diabetes
authors: Nicholls SJ, Pavo I, Bhatt DL, Buse JB, Del Prato S, Kahn SE, et al.
population: Modified intention-to-treat population of adults with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, after exclusion of 134 of 13,299 randomised who did not meet inclusion criteria; mean age 64.1 years, 29.0% women, mean BMI 32.6, mean HbA1c 8.4%
funder: Funded by Eli Lilly, as stated in the abstract; the sponsor's role was not read.
result: Active-comparator non-inferiority trial against dulaglutide 1.5 mg. Cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke occurred in 801 of 6586 (12.2%) on tirzepatide up to 15 mg against 862 of 6579 (13.1%) on dulaglutide (hazard ratio 0.92, 95.3% CI 0.83 to 1.01; non-inferiority P = 0.003, superiority P = 0.09). Adverse events appeared similar, with more gastrointestinal events on tirzepatide. The trial had no placebo group.
